title: Functoriality of framed equivariant instanton homology on the weakly admissible U(2)-cobordism category
author: Mike Miller Eismeier
source_version: arXiv:1907.01091v3 (CC BY 4.0); accepted for publication in Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society
difficulty_reason: Supplying the monograph's own analytical prerequisites - the moduli-package theorems (ModuliPackage, CobordismPackage, FamilyPackage), the transversality theorems trans1, trans2, trans3, the Uhlenbeck compactness theorem comp and the orientation results of Chapter 5 - still leaves a source-local assembly that is not a qualification exercise. The counted proof has to build the group I(Y,E,sigma;R) as a quotient of the direct sum over all regular perturbations carrying the signature datum sigma by the canonical isomorphisms rho_12 defined by paths of perturbations, verify that each inclusion of a summand is an isomorphism onto the quotient, prove that the chain map induced by a cobordism is independent of the regular perturbation extending the boundary data, and then check composition up to chain homotopy so that the construction really is a functor on the weakly admissible U(2)-cobordism category. Every one of those steps is carried by the book's own moduli-space, gluing and homotopy technology rather than by quoting a textbook, which places the unit well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations in gauge theory and low-dimensional topology.
